newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-CELTIC V RANGERS MATCH ANALYSIS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-CELTIC V RANGERS MATCH ANALYSIS.

text.p: A look at the strengths and weaknesses of Celtic and Rangers who meet in the Scottish premier division on Sunday (1500 GMT):

Playing style: Manager Tommy Burns has tightened up Celtic's defence with the recent acquisition of Italian Enrico Annio and has created a potent strike force with Jorge Cadete and Paolo di Canio in an aggressive 3-5-2 formation. Celtic, like Rangers, are often so much better than their opposition that players have more freedom to move and exploit spaces than they do in the more competitive English premier league, and the team's formation, like Rangers, is a fluid one.

Strengths: Di Canio and Cadete in attack have the pace, power and talent to unlock most defences. Celtic are a free-scoring team who have scored 85 goals this season. Young goalkeeper Simon Kerr has also given the defence added stability.

Weaknesses: A collective lack of discipline which has seen red cards shown to Celtic's players with the frequency of traffic police handing out fines to speeding drivers. In one six-match spell between September 14 and October 12 six different Celtic players were sent off. Their other collective weakness would appear to be a mental one. Do they really believe they are good enough to deprive Rangers of the title?

Motivation: A century of loathing towards the other half of the Old Firm usually makes the players blood flow faster when it is time to meet Rangers. Besides the entirely rational wish of achieving that little goal for the second time in 10 days, a win would narrow Rangers lead to just two points.

Playing style: Like Celtic, Rangers can play almost any formation they like and still win the majority of their domestic matches at a canter. Manager Walter Smith has seen his team score 111 goals in all matches so far this season. Against Celtic he is likely to play with a slightly more defensive lineup.

Strengths: Usually Rangers are full of confidence and self-belief generated by the fact that they know they have most of the best players in the league in their own team. Few can live with them for pace, movement off the ball and defensive covering. Their strengths are well known, but they are not as strong at the moment as they would like to be because of injuries and a recent run of poor results.

Weaknesses: Rangers are going into Sunday's match badly hit by injuries and a rare lack of confidence could be creeping into the side following three games without a win. They are missing long-term injuries Paul Gascoigne, Stuart McCall and new Chilean striker Sebastian Rozental and have worries over another six players.

Motivation: Besides the reciprocal hatred of Celtic, Rangers will be desperate to win -- or at the very least avoid defeat -- on Sunday. A win will take them eight points clear at the top, a draw will leave them a comfortable five points clear, but a defeat will bring Celtic to just two points behind. Rangers are already under enough pressure to win the title for the ninth successive season to match Celtic's record set between 1965 and 1974. Defeat at Celtic would only add to it.
